summary.text: Selvena N. Brooks-Powers represents the 31st District on the New York City Council, which includes Arverne, Edgemere, Far Rockaway, Laurelton, Rosedale and Springfield Gardens in Queens.
Her Council biography says she chairs the Committee on Criminal Justice and was the first Black woman to serve as the Council's Majority Whip.

paragraphs.text: Brooks-Powers is the daughter of Jamaican-born parents and a lifelong Southeast Queens resident, according to her Council biography.
She graduated from Wilberforce University and holds a master's degree in international law from New York University.
Before elected office she was a manager for M/WBE compliance, external affairs and community outreach on the JFK International Airport Redevelopment Program.

Earlier she was a communications director for SEIU campaigns, including the Fight for $15, and worked in the New York State Senate Majority Conference Leader's office, the Mayor's Office to Combat Domestic Violence and the first Public Advocate's Office.
The biography says she has directed over $470 million in capital and discretionary funds to her district and was the first chair of the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
